# odyssey-027 (6.1–109): review, pass 1 (units.json; gloss.json not read)

Method: notes checked label by label and position claim by position claim against the line; cross-references checked against the source JSON; Greek to `l` word by word; `l` to `i`; remembered-English check; quotation marks; house table and new-renderings.md; note length (all 21–109 words, none over 110; units 45 and 48 are under the 25-word band, warn only, left) and backticks. `t` untouched (verified identical before and after). Scansion flags: none, so no hand scan needed. Tally: 1 major, 5 minor, 9 nit.

## Changes (line · field · severity · wrong · done)

- 4 · n · major (gate) · a backtick in the note ("kept in `l`"), which the validator fails and the conventions forbid · replaced with "the word-for-word English keeps the literal sense".
- 20 (cites 21) · n · major (bad cross-reference) · "word for word 4.802": Murray's 4.802 is ἐς θάλαμον δ’ εἰσῆλθε …; στῆ δ’ ἄρ’ ὑπὲρ κεφαλῆς is 4.803 (the published unit starts at 802 and holds both lines) · changed to 4.803.
- 57 (line 58) · n · minor (label) · "takes a short-vowel subjunctive" said of ἄγωμαι, which has the long vowel and is an ordinary subjunctive · now "an ordinary subjunctive".
- 39 · n · minor (label) · κάλλιον called "used as an adverb"; it is the neuter predicate of an understood ἐστί · reworded.
- 51 · n · minor (label) · "unaugmented … (Attic ἐκιχήσατο)" implied an Attic form · now "the augmented form would be ἐκιχήσατο".
- 24 · n · minor (label) · προσέφη called the "reply-verb" though nothing has been said to the hearer (the new-renderings row itself refuses "answered") · now "the house verb 'addressed' (not 'answered': …)".
- 25 · n · nit · νύ described as "a particle of urgency" (not an LSJ sense) · now "the enclitic particle 'now, then', which sharpens the question".
- 19 · n · nit · ἐπέκειντο "is the usual way to say that a door is shut" (a claim about the poem's usage that this part cannot show) · now "here means that the doors were shut".
- 66 · n · nit · θαλερός glossed "lusty", a word the new-renderings row refuses · "flourishing".
- 79 · n · nit · ληκύθος given as the form; the text has ληκύθῳ · now "ληκύθῳ is the dative of ληκύθος".
- 34 · n · nit · μνῶνται note did not name its subject · added "and ἀριστῆες is its subject".
- 2 · i · nit (l/i) · "of the Phaeacians" dropped ἀνδρῶν · "of the Phaeacian men".
- 34 · l · minor · "you are wooed by the best men" made an active deponent (μνῶνται, subject ἀριστῆες) passive · "they are wooing you, the best men throughout the land".
- 34 · i · minor · i attached πάντων Φαιήκων to the best men, l attached it to the land (Greek allows both; the two layers must agree) · i now "the best men are courting you throughout the land of all the Phaeacians".
- 39 · l · minor · "For also for you" rendered καὶ δέ with "for" (γάρ), and disagreed with i and with line 60 ("And also") · "And also for you yourself".
- 53 · l · minor · "she came up, to go among the famous kings" made Nausicaa's coming up the purpose of going among the kings; μετὰ … ἐς βουλήν belongs to ἐρχομένῳ (the father); θύραζε also stood on the wrong l line · rebuilt: "and to him, out of doors / going, she came up, on his way among the famous kings / to the council, …". i already right.
- 68 · i · minor (remembered English) · "I do not begrudge you the mules, child, nor anything else." had the shape of a familiar published line · rebuilt from the genitive-of-the-thing construction: "Child, I begrudge you neither the mules nor anything else." (l unchanged).
- 85 (line 87) · i · nit · μάλα περ ῥυπόωντα "very dirty" became the superlative "filthiest" · "even very dirty things".
- 93 (line 94) · i · minor · ἀποπλύνεσκε is iterative (the note says so) and μάλιστα was rendered "most washed" · "where the sea especially used to wash the pebbles clean against the land".

The last unit of odyssey-026 (5.491–493) is narrative, so no speech runs in. The part ends in narrative, so none runs on. House epithets (πολύτλας δῖος, μεγαλήτωρ, θεοειδής, γλαυκῶπις, κλυτός/κλειτός "famous", ἀγαυοί, μάκαρες, μάστιξεν δ’ ἐλάαν) and the new-renderings rows are applied consistently, including ὑψηλὴν ἐύκυκλον identical at 58 and 70 and σιγαλόεντα "glossy" at 26, 38, 81. Position claims (ἐσθλή line-initial at 30; τοῦ first at 13; name last in the third line at 17; τε … τε; οὔτε ×3) and line cross-references (15, 19, 31, 58, 81, 86, 96, 102, 109; 3.484/3.494) all true.

## Findings refused

- 90 (line 91) · ἐσφόρεον μέλαν ὕδωρ: possibly the clothes, not the water, are what is carried in (to the water). Refused: the note already states both readings and takes water as the object; the grammar alone does not settle it and I have no lexicon text to decide. Left for the owner's judgement.
- 90 (line 92) · "each trying to outdo the other" might be remembered English. Refused: it is the ratified new-renderings row, built from ἔρις "rivalry" + προφέρω "put forward", and I could not identify a source.
- 85 (line 86) · i "where the washing-places were" vs l "there indeed were": the first ἔνθα is relative in i and demonstrative in l. Refused: both are legitimate readings of an asyndeton and the sense is identical.
- 4 · note says ὑπερηνορέω is "over-manly" while `l` says "over-bold". Refused: the note gives the etymology, `l` the house rendering; not a contradiction.
- 57/71 · "more elevated" i wording ("will you not" for οὐκ ἂν … ἐφοπλίσσειας, "gave orders" for ἐκέκλετο): within house rows, left.
- Notes at units 45 and 48 are under the 25-word warn band: a warn, not a cap; the notes say what is needed.
- 102 · i "along the very long ridge of Taygetus": "ridge" is an addition but harmless. Refused.
- 79 · i "Her mother also gave": "also" and "her" are inferences from the change of subject already stated in the note. Refused.

Second pass (gloss.json parse check) still to do.
